title: Scheme-isomorphism squares for arbitrary finite coefficient maps
statement: For finite commutative rings A,B and any ring homomorphism phi:A->B, schemes T,X,Z,S, a map f:T->X, a closed immersion i:Z->X, a quasi-compact structure map aX:X->S with fixed compactification c, and a representative-normalized pro-etale scalar tensorator mu on X, all eight geometric properties of [def-sf-finite-free-coefficient-comparison-data] hold: DirectGeometry(phi,f), HomGeometry(phi,X), ClosedGeometry(phi,i), ExceptionalGeometry(phi,c,unit), ProDirectGeometry(phi,f), ProClosedGeometry(phi,i), ProHomGeometry(phi,X,mu), and ProOmegaGeometry(phi,c). This asserts equalities of the canonical maps, not invertibility of scalar comparisons or flatness of phi. Hom and direct/closed squares retain exactly the finite-Tor constructible domains of those definitions; the dualizing square evaluates at the regular unit.

source.place: Final paragraph: the constructions use only pullback, tensor, evaluation and natural adjunction maps, hence commute with scheme isomorphisms.

proof.text: Reindex the two small sites by a scheme isomorphism and its inverse. This gives exact module equivalences preserving constant ring actions and K-flat representatives. The scalar/geometric tensor square is the pure-tensor balancing equality before localization; hence it holds after deriving for every coefficient homomorphism, including nonflat quotients.

Transpose the direct-image square under inverse image/direct image. Naturality of the counit and the scalar/geometric square give the same transpose. Transpose again for closed support under its actual direct-image/right-adjoint adjunction. The image comparison inverse terms cancel on the isomorphism domain; reindexing preserves that domain, and both inverse extensions are zero off it. The compact-support comparison is the proper/open composite; apply the same naturality calculation and take its counit mate for ExceptionalGeometry.

For Hom apply tensor--Hom transposition: both paths are scalar extension of pulled-back evaluation. The normalized tensorators are the same descended balancing maps, so uniqueness of transpose gives the specified equality. Evaluating the compact-support mate at the regular unit gives the dualizing equality.

The site/scalar and site/geometric balancing squares commute. Taking right mates includes the site counit and identifies rnuScalar and rnuPull. Substitution in proClosedMap/proClosedPull and proOmegaMap/proOmegaPull transfers the etale squares. On finite-Tor constructible inputs use bounded etale origin when needed. The evaluation transpose also proves the pro-etale Hom equality for every representative-normalized tensorator.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficient_map_geometric_squares
    (A B : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {T X Z S : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ X)
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    {aX : X ⟶ S} [QuasiCompact aX] (c : Compactification aX)
    (μ : Sites.TensorComparison true φ X) (hμ : Sites.NormalizedTensor true φ X μ) :
    Sites.DirectGeometry φ f ∧ Sites.HomGeometry φ X ∧
    Sites.ClosedGeometry φ i ∧ Sites.ExceptionalGeometry φ c (𝟙_ _) ∧
    Sites.ProDirectGeometry φ f ∧ Sites.ProClosedGeometry φ i ∧
    Sites.ProHomGeometry φ X μ ∧ Sites.ProOmegaGeometry φ c
